subtopics.title: Choosing the Ratio, and Finding a Side on Top

questions.question: Which side keeps its name no matter which acute angle you choose?
options: The hypotenuse — it is always opposite the right angle

questions.question: A 20 m ladder leans at 35° to the ground. Which ratio gives the height reached on the wall?
options: Sine — the height is opposite and the ladder is the hypotenuse
Tangent — the height is opposite and the ladder is adjacent

questions.question: That height, to two decimal places, is:
Why can the side opposite an acute angle never exceed the hypotenuse?
options: Because the angle is less than 90°
Because the adjacent side is always longer
Because the sine of any acute angle is less than one

questions.question: cos 40° = 15 ÷ x. To solve for x you:
The cable anchored 15 m from the mast foot at 40° has length:
An answer of 11,49 m for that cable can be rejected immediately because:
options: Cables must be whole numbers of metres
The hypotenuse must be longer than the 15 m adjacent side

questions.question: The habit stated for this case is:
options: Unknown on top, multiply; unknown underneath, divide the known side by the ratio
Convert every ratio to sine first

subtopics.title: Finding Angles, and Solving the Whole Triangle

questions.question: A clinic ramp rises 800 mm over a horizontal run of 5 m. The angle of the ramp is:
The other acute angle in that triangle is:
The ramp surface itself (the third side) is best found by:
options: Pythagoras — √(0,8² + 5²) = 5,06 m, which inherits no rounding error

questions.question: The first step in that problem, before any ratio is chosen, is to:
options: Convert 800 mm to 0,8 m so both sides use one unit system
Switch the calculator to radian mode

questions.question: Angles of elevation and depression are measured from:
options: The nearest side of the triangle

questions.question: The learner stands 24 m from the mast, eyes 1,6 m up, elevation 62°. The mast's height is:
From a 40 m cliff the angle of depression to a boat is 25°. The boat's distance from the cliff foot is:
Why does the angle of depression from the cliff top equal the angle of elevation from the boat?
options: The two horizontals are parallel, so the angles are alternate angles
Because tangent is the same for both

subtopics.title: Naming the Sides from Where You Stand

questions.question: In the room-corner picture, the 'long diagonal to the far corner' stands for:
Moving to the other acute angle in a triangle:
options: Swaps opposite and adjacent, which is why the angle is chosen before labelling

questions.question: When choosing a ratio you should look at:
options: Only two sides — the one you know and the one you want

subtopics.title: Upstairs You Multiply, Downstairs You Divide

questions.question: The bread analogy (12 loaves for R216, or R18 each) is used to show that:
options: Which operation you use depends on which quantity is missing
Division is always safer than multiplication
Ratios must be rounded before use

questions.question: In sin 35° = h ÷ 20, the unknown is upstairs, so:
The free safety net for hypotenuse answers is:
options: Checking the calculator is in radian mode
Confirming the hypotenuse came out as the longest side in the triangle

questions.question: For the mast cable, adjacent 15 m and angle 40°, the answer 19,58 m arises because:
options: The triangle was solved with Pythagoras
The unknown hypotenuse sat downstairs, so 15 was divided by cos 40°

questions.question: The learner's triangle in the mast problem starts:
options: At her eyes, 1,6 m above the ground — so 1,6 m must be added at the end
At her feet, so nothing is added
At the top of the mast
At the midpoint of the 24 m

questions.question: The rise above her eye level, 24 × tan 62°, equals:
The suggested cure for confusion about a depression angle is to:
options: Move yourself to the bottom of the picture and use the same number as an elevation

questions.question: Placing the 25° angle of depression inside the triangle at the cliff-top vertex is wrong because:
options: The triangle is not right-angled there
It should be measured from the sea
The interior angle at that vertex is its complement, 65°
